projects.name: dev-prune
projects.tagline: Gigabytes back. Nothing you can't rebuild.
projects.summary: A Rust CLI that reclaims the disk space idle repositories are holding in node_modules, .venv, target and vendor directories. It deletes one only after verifying read-only that the project's lockfile can rebuild it, and the same binary restores what it removed.

projects.name: LoginLens
projects.tagline: A local-only map of how you sign in to everything.
projects.summary: A browser extension that records which account, OAuth provider and MFA method you used on each site — the layer above passwords that nothing else tracks. It never asks for, reads or stores a password, and runs entirely on-device with no server and no account.

projects.name: Chronos-Ledger
projects.tagline: Campus scheduling and attendance, self-hosted and offline-first.
projects.summary: A self-hosted campus timetable and attendance stack that replaces paper registers and spreadsheet timetables. It runs entirely on a campus intranet with Docker as its only runtime dependency, and keeps working read-only — queueing writes — when the network drops.

projects.name: EquiLens
projects.tagline: Black-box bias detection for local language models.
projects.summary: A bias-auditing framework that probes any Ollama-compatible language model purely through its input/output interface, with no access to weights. It generates demographically paired prompts, runs them concurrently against a local model, and reports statistically analysed differences in the responses.

projects.name: Code-Ledger
projects.tagline: Your DSA grind, on your GitHub. Automatically.
projects.summary: A browser extension that commits every accepted competitive-programming solution to your own GitHub repository — code, problem statement and an optional AI review — with no extra steps after install. Practice that used to vanish into a judge's servers becomes a reviewable history.

projects.name: PulseWard-HMS
projects.summary: Licensed proprietary software developed under a commercial licence. The repository is private, so this entry records the work rather than linking to public source — details available on request.

projects.name: Vectra-180
projects.tagline: A dual-fisheye dashcam for the Pi Compute Module 5.
projects.summary: A headless dashcam that records continuously from a dual-fisheye USB camera, protects the footage around an impact, and serves clips to a phone over Wi-Fi. Because the two lenses sit a fixed distance apart it can also compute a depth map — on request, never while a clip is being written.

projects.name: cspell-sync
projects.summary: A VS Code extension that keeps cSpell custom words in sync between every project and the global dictionary, in both directions. Words added in one project reach the global list within a second, so opening a new project no longer means red squiggles under your whole technical vocabulary.

projects.name: Facial-Emotion-Detector
projects.tagline: Facial emotion classification from landmark geometry.
projects.summary: A facial emotion recognition pipeline that detects faces, extracts MediaPipe landmarks, and classifies the expression from landmark geometry rather than raw pixels. It ships the full workflow — image collection, dataset preparation, training and inference — as scripted steps.

projects.name: RanobeGemini
projects.tagline: AI reading companion for web novels and fanfiction.
projects.summary: A local-first browser extension that improves the readability of machine-translated web novels, summarises long chapters in place, and tracks a reading library across several sites. It works with Gemini, any OpenAI-compatible endpoint, or a local Ollama model.

projects.name: ViewFlare
projects.tagline: Serverless view counter and SVG badges on Cloudflare.
projects.summary: A serverless telemetry counter for projects and documentation, built on Cloudflare Workers and D1 with a Hono API. One POST increments a project's views and one image URL renders a live SVG badge, so a repository gets usage counts without anyone running a backend. Formerly published as CFlair-Counter.

projects.name: the-pensive-index
projects.tagline: Discovery-first fanfiction search with prompt generation.
projects.summary: A fanfiction discovery platform that searches existing tagged stories against complex, nuanced criteria before offering to generate a prompt. Tags are hierarchical with conditional branching rather than flat, so a search can express a specific premise instead of a keyword.

projects.name: SignLanguageDetector
projects.tagline: Sign language recognition, collection to browser inference.
projects.summary: An end-to-end sign language recognition project: collect images, build a dataset, train a classifier, and serve real-time predictions in the browser from webcam hand landmarks. It also exposes a headless REST endpoint and swaps trained models without a restart.

projects.name: ToxicGuard_AI
projects.tagline: On-device toxic language detection in the browser.
projects.summary: A cross-browser Manifest V3 extension that flags or censors toxic language as it is typed, using TensorFlow.js and the toxicity model loaded inside the content script. Classification happens on the device, so the text being checked never leaves the browser.

projects.name: Save-Sync
projects.tagline: Save points for code, for when git is overkill.
projects.summary: A checkpoint tool for projects where full version control is more ceremony than the work deserves — experiments, tutorials and quick prototypes. It snapshots a project's state and restores it, so a risky change can be undone without a branching model.

projects.name: ActionsCounter
projects.tagline: Project analytics running on GitHub Actions alone.
projects.summary: An event counter that runs entirely inside GitHub Actions, tracking usage, downloads or API calls through webhook pings. It stores counts in GitHub Variables, a database, or a repository, so a project gets analytics without provisioning any infrastructure.

projects.name: BreachCheck
projects.tagline: Check credentials against known breaches, privately.
projects.summary: A tool for checking whether credentials appear in known data breaches without disclosing what is being checked, using k-anonymity range queries so only a short hash prefix ever leaves the machine.

projects.name: docs-rag
projects.tagline: Retrieval-augmented QA that refuses to guess.
projects.summary: A retrieval-augmented question answering system over documents you choose — PDFs, Markdown, HTML, Wikipedia and GitHub files. It answers only from those documents, cites what it used, and refuses when they do not contain the answer, with that refusal verified mechanically rather than merely requested in the prompt.

projects.name: HiveXplore
projects.tagline: A Hive blockchain social client, built in 36 hours.
projects.summary: A hackathon build for IIT Delhi CodeHive: a social client that reads posts, profiles and wallet history straight off the Hive blockchain and broadcasts new posts back to it. It is here as evidence of working against a chain rather than as a product.
